note: Window agent m1600-m1501, 2 Nov 2026. Three keyframe overrides, no events, no rulings. (1) First Sealand dynasty: the -1600 keyframe adds a 42-50 E x 27-32.3 N rectangle (1,599 cells, 404,000 km2) to Cliopatria's 13,101 km2 marsh shape: northern Arabia, Kuwait and Khuzestan, which no page gives the Sealand. m1700-m1601 (keyframe_overrides/0) already replaced the -1700 keyframe by Cliopatria's marsh core plus Dhi-Qar, Basra, and discs on Uruk, Nippur and Isin (179 cells), so the anchor at -1600 holds that land; this keyframe now carries the same region (Cliopatria's -1600 core) and equals the anchor. (2) Babylonia: babylonia_-1600 subtracts the same rectangle from Cliopatria's shape (269 of its 506 cells, including the land north of the Sealand's); it now subtracts only the corrected Sealand land, which hands Babylonia 140 cells back at -1600 (155 less a 15-cell Muthanna exclave cut by the reviewer), a snap that this patch explains (babylonia_-1700 in m1700-m1601 still carries the rectangle). (3) Minoan civilization: Cliopatria's Crete shape (16 of the island's 27 cells) leaves out Phaistos and Kydonia (Chania), both named by the page, so it becomes the island, as the dossier's own founding event has it. Neighbour windows: the rectangle is still in first-sealand-dynasty_-1500 and babylonia_-1500, and the Cliopatria Crete shape in minoan-civilization_-1500; all start in m1500-m1401.

correction.text: the marsh core at the head of the Gulf plus the Dhi-Qar and Basra governorates (Girsu, Lagash, Ur, Larsa), Uruk, and Nippur and Isin: 'Sealand pottery has been found at Girsu, Uruk, and Lagash but in no site north of that'; Ilum-ma-ili 'is thought to have conquered Nippur late in Samsu-iluna's reign'

keyframe_overrides.why: Same region as m1700-m1601 keyframe_overrides/0 (Cliopatria's -1600 core instead of its -1700 one). The page's only evidence of extent is pottery: 'Sealand pottery has been found at Girsu, Uruk, and Lagash but in no site north of that', with Ur's neighbourhood (Tell Sakhariya 'a few miles east of Ur') and offerings to 'Inanna of Larsa' under Ayadaragalama; Ilum-ma-ili 'is thought to have conquered Nippur late in Samsu-iluna's reign'. The dossier's -1600 correction instead adds the 42-50 E x 27-32.3 N rectangle (404,000 km2), which takes northern Arabia, Kuwait and Elam's Khuzestan (122 cells that the size rule gave the Sealand in the published draft). [Reviewer: the correction text quoted 'Nippur recognized Ilum-ma-ili as king', which is the Samsu-iluna page's sentence ('by the time of Samsu-iluna's death, Nippur recognized Ilum-ma-ili as king', https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samsu-iluna, checked), not this page's; the text now quotes this page. Isin rests on the Samsu-iluna page ('Records keep going in Nippur and Isin until Samsu-iluna's 29th year, and then cease there as well') via the -1700 anchor.]

the desert of Al-Muthanna south of Ur and Uruk, which the Sealand's Dhi-Qar and Uruk cut off from Babylonia

correction.text: Babylonia without the Sealand-held south (the corrected Sealand land: Dhi-Qar, Basra, Uruk, Nippur and Isin) and without the Muthanna desert beyond it

keyframe_overrides.why: Complement of the Sealand override. The dossier subtracts the whole 42-50 E x 27-32.3 N rectangle from Cliopatria's Babylonia (269 of 506 cells), but the Sealand page finds its pottery 'in no site north of' Girsu, Uruk and Lagash, so Babylonia keeps Cliopatria's shape everywhere except the land the Sealand holds. [Reviewer: Cliopatria's Babylonia minus the Sealand left a 15-cell Babylonian exclave in Al-Muthanna (45.6-46.44 E, 30.34-30.76 N), south of Sealand-held Ur and Uruk and cut off from Babylonia; no page gives Babylonia land beyond the Sealand, so the Muthanna cells are cut too (373 cells, against 388).]

correction.text: the island of Crete: Knossos, Phaistos, Zakros and Malia, and Kydonia (Chania) in the west

keyframe_overrides.why: The page lists the Neopalatial palaces 'at Knossos, Phaistos, Zakros, and Malia' and 'Kydonia (modern Chania), the only palatial site in West Crete'. Cliopatria's shape holds 16 of Crete's 27 cells and leaves out Phaistos (south) and Kydonia (west). The page cautions that 'it is unclear whether there was ever a unified Minoan state', but the dossier's own founding event and its -1450 end both use the whole island.
